items.content:
Meet Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash ⚡️

We’ve made the model more cost-effective, bumped the video generation and editing limit up to 15 seconds, and made updates to how scenes hold together over time. We've also given character speech an upgrade, reduced visual glitches like jump cuts, and made sure the model stays even truer to any reference assets you upload.

So… what does all of that actually mean for you?

It gives you more room to tell your story. With up to 15 seconds to work with, you have more flexibility to create what you need — videos look more cinematic and smooth, offering stronger consistency that keeps objects anchored from start to finish. And when characters speak, the dialogue sounds more fluid and natural.

Creators and everyday users can start directing scenes and multi-turn edits in @FlowbyGoogle, generating 15-second clips at no additional cost in Google Vids, or creating 15-second videos in the @GeminiApp. Plus, for developers and businesses building with the API, we've dropped the price by 30% from the previous generation, making it available at just $0.07 per second for 720p video.

Watch the model in action as it turns a single style frame into a 4-shot, 15-second macro science explainer of a living beehive ↓

Get started today:
— Creatives and Consumers: Direct and edit in Google Flow (rolling out), generate clips in Google Vids, or create videos in the Gemini App (rolling out to all Google AI subscribers, with 15-second clips available to Ultra)
— Developers: Prototype in @GoogleAIStudio
— Enterprises and businesses: Try Omni in Gemini for Business and scale campaigns in Google Ads
https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/introducing-gemini-omni-1-2-flash/

en.summary: Google released an upgraded Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash model, reducing inference costs and extending video generation duration to 15 seconds, while improving character voice and scene consistency.

items.content:
ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base just dropped! Time to open that project folder. 🚀

Our efficient sparse MoE language model draws on data spanning multiple domains and languages, achieving SOTA on multiple benchmarks among similarly sized base models. Its architecture and training system were designed together for efficient training and inference, with advances in attention mechanisms, expert routing, and training objectives:
- 280B total parameters; 14B activated per token
- Pre-trained on 33.5T tokens
- Up to 1M-token context for fine-tuning and inference
- FP8 and BF16 weights

The weights come straight from pre-training, with no mid- or post-training. Compare methods from the same checkpoint, measure what each adds, and shape the model around your own tasks.

Explore ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base here 👇
ERNIE Blog: https://ernie.baidu.com/release/ernie-5-5-flash-base/
Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/baidu/ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Base

items.title: Our security researchers built an autonomous cyber vulnerability discovery, exploitation, and patching pipeline.
items.summary: OpenAI 安全研究團隊打造自主網路漏洞挖掘與修補流程，利用即將推出的專用模型成功驗證並修補 948 個 Linux 核心漏洞，展示 AI 代理在資安防禦上的實戰潛力。
items.content:
Our security researchers built an autonomous cyber vulnerability discovery, exploitation, and patching pipeline.

In a single run with an upcoming cyber model, it validated and generated patches for 948 local privilege escalation vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel at a total API cost of $1.2 million.

The pipeline finds security-relevant code, scans for vulnerabilities, reproduces them in isolated environments, tests whether they can be exploited, and generates candidate patches.

Human researchers review the results before reporting vulnerabilities and propose fixes to maintainers.

The run reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities. It produced proofs of concept for 291 information leaks and working exploits for 948 distinct local privilege escalation vulnerabilities.

Those exploits worked on a stock Linux desktop configuration with standard security protections enabled.

The full run cost $1,213,430 in API credits—about $1,279 per distinct local privilege escalation vulnerability.

For context, applying historical Pwn2Own and TyphoonPWN bounty rates gives a hypothetical value of $18.9M–$66.3M.

This demonstrates the relative efficacy of using AI models for securing software—defenders should proactively analyze software to make cyber attacks cost-prohibitive.

The agents also discovered and used at least 10 Linux exploitation techniques that, to the best of our knowledge and all of the experts that we consulted, are novel.

This suggests frontier LLMs can discover and patch new approaches to exploitation, beyond simply applying known techniques.

Our goal is to help defenders find and fix vulnerabilities before attackers can use them. We’re working with Linux maintainers and Patch the Planet partners on reports and patches.

https://openai.com/index/a-thousand-fewer-paths-to-root/

en.summary: The OpenAI security research team built an autonomous cyber vulnerability discovery and patching pipeline, leveraging an upcoming dedicated model to successfully verify and patch 948 Linux kernel vulnerabilities, demonstrating the real-world potential of AI agents in cybersecurity defense.

items.title: We’re sharing how our biology research team worked with Claude to map the first 3D structure of a vault particle from bacterial life.
items.summary: Anthropic 分享其生物研究團隊如何結合 Claude 首次解析出細菌穹窿體（vault particle）的 3D 結構，展現 LLM 協助推進基礎科學與結構生物學研究的潛力。
items.content:
We’re sharing how our biology research team worked with Claude to map the first 3D structure of a vault particle from bacterial life.

Vault particles are a longstanding mystery. They are barrel-shaped objects, among the largest protein structures found in our cells. They were first discovered by Leonard Rome and Nancy Kedersha in 1986, but their function remains unknown.

With Claude, we’ve found results that might bring us closer to solving that mystery.

Until now, vaults were only known in the cells of complex things like animals and plants. We have shown that similar proteins from bacteria (and the viruses that infect them) can also assemble into vaults. Finding the structures in these simpler forms of life may make it easier to investigate their function in our own cells.

For our life sciences team, the project was also a demonstration of the potential (and the limitations) of using AI to accelerate science.

In our full piece, we discuss how Claude was able to dramatically speed up some stages—manually determining the vault particle’s structure would have taken weeks to months of painstaking work, but here it took days. We also discuss how Claude made some simple mistakes along the way, and how we collaborated with our machine learning researchers to address them.

Read more: https://www.anthropic.com/research/investigating-vault-particles-with-claude

Read the full preprint here: https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/76e55fbe85697afbaae16b839498dc00797dec30.pdf https://x.com/AnthropicAI/status/2118073667858887068/photo/1

en.summary: Anthropic shared how its biology research team used Claude to resolve the 3D structure of bacterial vault particles for the first time, demonstrating the potential of LLMs to advance fundamental science and structural biology research.

items.title: Kolibri can reason at four efforts: none, low, medium, and high. Our SFT training traces didn't have effort labels, so we had to label th...

items.content:
Kolibri can reason at four efforts: none, low, medium, and high. Our SFT training traces didn't have effort labels, so we had to label them post-hoc.

A new blog post by @L_Salewski explains how we did this, with interactive figures 🧵 https://x.com/Aleph__Alpha/status/2117633164851995038/video/1

A simple baseline is one pair of length thresholds to bucket each sample into one of three reasoning efforts. It fails because reasoning length follows the domain: 49% of chat would be low and 83% of math high.

Drag the thresholds anywhere and some domain stays lopsided. https://x.com/Aleph__Alpha/status/2117633167746343055/video/1

So every dataset gets its own 30th and 70th percentile, as a cheap stand-in for its domain.

Across 74 datasets the median trace runs from 27 to 90K tokens. https://x.com/Aleph__Alpha/status/2117633171298910525/video/1

Inside one dataset, difficulty still spreads the reasoning length. We used an LLM judge distilled into a 2B grader to rate every prompt either easy, medium, or hard.

Each of the 176 (dataset, difficulty) groups then gets its own thresholds. https://x.com/Aleph__Alpha/status/2117633174994112750/video/1

A hard cut at the thresholds would teach the model a token count to stop at. So the label is drawn softly around them, and each group still ends up close to 30% low, 40% medium, 30% high. https://x.com/Aleph__Alpha/status/2117633179150643567/video/1

Does it work? On the SFT checkpoint, reasoning length orders low < medium < high on 23 of 24 benchmarks. At a fixed effort, hard prompts still get 32.5 times the reasoning of easy ones.

After RL, the released model keeps 98% of its high score at low, with 76% of the tokens. https://x.com/Aleph__Alpha/status/2117633183055577529/video/1

The post has the full method, what RL adds on top, and the open problems. You can even set the post's own reasoning effort, adapting its length!

Blog: https://aleph-alpha.com/en/blog/reasoning-effort-that-adapts-to-the-request/
Tech report: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31945

Thanks to @L_Salewski and the SFT team.

en.summary: Aleph Alpha published a technical blog post detailing how training data was annotated across four reasoning effort levels for Kolibri to achieve more flexible reasoning capabilities.

items.title: Parsy is currently the best parsing model in the world.
items.summary: Aleph Alpha 推出文檔解析模型 Parsy，在 ParseBench 等多項基準測試中超越現有方案取得 SOTA 表現。
items.content:
Parsy is currently the best parsing model in the world.  

Read on for how we built this model on top of our parsing harness. 🧵 https://x.com/Aleph__Alpha/status/2115824114153730229/photo/1

In the sixth round of training and label cleaning, the model passed the harness.  

Our explanation for the model overtaking the harness: the latter got its quality at run time by combining models and catching their mistakes on every page. The model instead learns from the cleaned result of that process.

Parsy is SOTA on multiple benchmarks like ParseBench, fr-bench-pdf2md, or olmOCR-bench. https://x.com/Aleph__Alpha/status/2115824121359843754/photo/1

We re-ran ParseBench with the public scoring code, and the open-weight models matched the leaderboard while LlamaParse initially did not. @llama_index traced the gap and refreshed the scores the same day, and is adding scheduled runs so anyone can reproduce the leaderboard. https://x.com/Aleph__Alpha/status/2115824125117866003/photo/1

Knowing where every element sits on the page makes the model useful beyond extraction. For example, for source validation in chat assistants.

As Parsy keeps the bounding box of every element, an answer can point to the exact region on the page it came from.

Read the full post by @ABCalec, @yassinekh67, and Lukas Tatge: https://aleph-alpha.com/en/blog/parsy-distilling-an-agentic-parsing-harness/

en.summary: Aleph Alpha introduced Parsy, a document parsing model that outperforms existing solutions to achieve SOTA performance across benchmarks like ParseBench.

items.title: How does the community evaluate multilingual capabilities of LLMs? Mostly by translating evaluation datasets, since most of them are pred...
items.summary: Aleph Alpha 檢視 30 個英語評測基準的德語翻譯版本，揭示翻譯與文化差異對多語言 LLM 評估準確性造成的負面影響。
items.content:
How does the community evaluate multilingual capabilities of LLMs? Mostly by translating evaluation datasets, since most of them are predominantly in English. How does translation change what the eval actually measures? https://x.com/Aleph__Alpha/status/2115096230300987763/photo/1

We reviewed thirty German translations of English evals and found three types of errors: incorrect translations, grammatical mismatches, and foreign cultural context.

Translation errors mean that the eval no longer matches the original question. Grammatical mismatches often mean that the question and the answers no longer agree and may even give away the correct answer. Better automatic translation techniques largely solve these two problems.

Foreign cultural context is the harder problem. Questions about another country’s laws still test that country’s culture, but in German. A translation often implicitly decides what that cultural context is, influencing what that eval measures.

As model builders for German-speaking users, we believe this choice should be ours to make. Read more in our new blog by Alejandro, Raziye, Prabhu, @frankstefansch1, and Martin: https://aleph-alpha.com/en/blog/translated-words-untranslated-meaning/

en.summary: Aleph Alpha examined German translations of 30 English benchmarks, uncovering the negative impact of translation artifacts and cultural disparities on multilingual LLM evaluation accuracy.

items.title: The location of one space in a multiple-choice evaluation changes what it measures. It changes the probability of the correct answer by s...
items.summary: Aleph Alpha 探討選擇題評測中空格位置對模型預測機率的巨大影響，指出 LLM 評估基準可能存在顯著敏感性與偏差。
items.content:
The location of one space in a multiple-choice evaluation changes what it measures. It changes the probability of the correct answer by several orders of magnitude but usually barely changes the accuracy.

Multiple-Choice (MC) evals end the prompt with an “Answer:” and compute the probability of the labels A to D. The space after the colon can go to two places: end of the prompt as “Answer: “ or at the start of the label “ B”.

Research has found that this simple choice has an impact on the performance. Putting the space in the choices results in higher performance, but it is unclear why.

Every tokenizer we tested turns the string “Answer: B” into tokens like “Answer”, “:” “ B” - the space and the choice go together as a single token. In pre-training data, a standalone space followed by a bare ‘B’ is four to five orders of magnitude rarer.

What does this mean? A prompt that forces the model to predict a bare “B” has seen far lesser training data to learn from. As a result, the probability of the correct answer drops by several orders of magnitude across Olmo 3, Qwen3.5, and Gemma 4 on ARC, MMLU and PIQA.

Accuracy barely changes. Despite the drastic change in probabilities, in six out of nine model-benchmark pairs, there is less than a 0.5pp change. So, where does the probability go?

Given a prompt that ends with a space, we find that Olmo 3 still generates an answer with a space and is semantically correct 90% of the time.

Our recommendation is to split the prompt and the answer so that the tokens match what the model is trained with. This can be checked before any inference, with just a tokenizer: tokenizing the prompt and answer separately should give the same tokens as tokenizing them together. Read the full blog here: https://aleph-alpha.com/en/blog/mind-the-tokenizer/

en.summary: Aleph Alpha explored the dramatic impact of whitespace placement on model prediction probabilities in multiple-choice benchmarks, pointing out significant sensitivities and biases in LLM evaluation frameworks.

items.title: New Anthropic research: progress on provable inference for large language models.
items.summary: Anthropic 發表 FlashProve 技術研究，利用密碼學證明實現高效率的可驗證推論（provable inference），確保使用者取得未遭篡改的指定模型回覆。
items.content:
New Anthropic research: progress on provable inference for large language models.

Here, we introduce FlashProve. Building on established cryptographic techniques, FlashProve allows developers to verify whether a given response came from a given AI model. It’s substantially more efficient than prior open-source methods for doing so. 

These proofs have a range of applications. They can, for instance, make it harder for attackers to hijack a chat, or enable safety evaluators to verify that the model they’re testing is the same one being served to customers.

For our full write-up, see here: https://www.anthropic.com/research/provable-inference

Further progress in provable inference will likely be an important part of improving trust in AI deployment. To that end, we're open-sourcing FlashProve’s code, here: https://github.com/anthropics/FlashProve

We’re grateful to our collaborators: Alessandro Chiesa, @GiacomoFenzi, @gwberg95, @miranda__christ, Rahul Dalal (http://rdalal.github.io) and Ben Mayer (@transmissions11).

en.summary: Anthropic published research on FlashProve, utilizing cryptographic proofs to achieve efficient verifiable inference (provable inference) and ensure users receive tamper-proof outputs from the specified model.

items.title: Can LLMs track state changes over long texts—like an object changing hands or a variable reassignment?
items.summary: Ai2 發表評估基準 StateBench，測試顯示前沿語言模型在長文本複雜狀態追蹤任務上的準確率大幅下降。
items.content:
Can LLMs track state changes over long texts—like an object changing hands or a variable reassignment?

On our new StateBench eval, frontier models including GPT-6 Sol & Claude Opus 5.5 fell to 13% accuracy or lower on the hardest, longest problems. 🧵

https://github.com/allenai/state-bench https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2117670295339171994/video/1

StateBench separates state tracking into 4 levels: r-trivial, aperiodic, soluble, & general finite.

These range from problems like remembering something fixed, such as a birth date, to harder ones like tracking a ball as cups are repeatedly swapped.

We tested open pretrained models + frontier models incl. Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5, & GPT-6 Sol + Luna.

Frontier models did well on simpler problems. But as tasks got harder & inputs longer, accuracy dropped sharply—to 13% or lower on the longest general finite problems. https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2117670297532797227/photo/1

To test whether failures came from architecture or pretraining, we trained LLMs directly on StateBench, then evaled them on longer inputs.

Hybrids + Gated DeltaNets were near-perfect on the first 3 levels; transformers degraded with length & couldn’t solve general finite. https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2117670299298599001/photo/1

On StateBench’s hardest level, a flexible Gated DeltaNet handled sequences ~10× longer than those seen in training.

Our new proof shows that even Gated DeltaNet with non-negative eigenvalues can solve some periodic tasks under fixed-precision arithmetic with rounding.

We’re releasing StateBench so researchers can test new models, extend our work, & build better state-tracking data.

Explore more in our blog: https://allenai.org/blog/statebench
Download the dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/state-bench

en.summary: Ai2 released the StateBench evaluation benchmark, where tests revealed a significant drop in frontier LLMs' accuracy on complex long-context state-tracking tasks.

items.title: Sakana AI Symposium: Building the Future of Language Models, World Models, and Physical AI from Japan
items.summary: Sakana AI 發布研討會英文回顧，探討語言模型、世界模型與具身實體 AI 的未來發展。
items.content:
Sakana AI Symposium: Building the Future of Language Models, World Models, and Physical AI from Japan

Event Report (English): https://sakana.ai/symposium-2026/#English 

On October 26, we hosted the symposium “From World Models to Real-World AI” at Hitotsubashi Hall in Tokyo. More than 400 people joined us for a keynote by Professor Jürgen Schmidhuber (@SchmidhuberAI), who became our Chief Scientific Advisor in September, and a conversation with our CEO David Ha, his co-author on the 2018 paper “World Models.”

In his keynote, Jürgen traced the path to today’s AI through the work of researchers around the world, including Shun-ichi Amari and Kunihiko Fukushima in Japan, as well as his own 1990 work on world models and artificial curiosity.

Our Chief Scientist Takuya Akiba also introduced “Sakana Sawara” (provisional name), a new language model series we are building from scratch, starting with pre-training. If everything goes smoothly, the first model, a small model called “Sawara Small” (provisional name), will be released in spring 2027.

Perhaps half of the AI Jürgen has envisioned has been realized through generative AI. The other half, artificial scientists that design their own experiments and physical AI that works in the real world, has yet to scale. We believe that opportunity lies especially outside the big labs, and that Japan is one of the most promising places to pursue it. We hope this symposium becomes a starting point for shaping the next era of AI in Japan, together with companies and research institutions across the country.

Videos will be added later. A big thank you to everyone who joined us! 🐟

items.title: We asked Mistral Large 4 to show what happens when you break a molecule. ⚛️
items.summary: Mistral AI 展示 Mistral Large 4 自行編寫量子化學求解器並建構 3D 分子可視化應用的強大能力。
items.content:
We asked Mistral Large 4 to show what happens when you break a molecule. ⚛️

With a short prompt, it wrote a quantum chemistry SCF solver from scratch, validated its output, and built a 3D view around it. 

Le Chonk also understand chemistry enough to independently choose how to break the molecule and what orbitals to show, without further input. 🧵

Step 1️⃣: the solver:
It computes single-electron orbitals, which predict where electrons can be found. 

Step 2️⃣: the visualisation. 
Drag the slider: the bond fades, the orbitals split onto the two fragments, the energy climbs. You watch the molecule break.

For those of us who don’t do quantum chemistry before coffee ☕: 

this is how chemists predict how a molecule behaves on a computer, before testing it in a lab. It’s a first step toward new drugs, materials or batteries. 

Le Chonk wrote the tool from scratch, and it gets the right answers.

en.summary: Mistral AI showcased Mistral Large 4's powerful ability to independently write a quantum chemistry solver and build a 3D molecular visualization app.

items.content:
Sakana AIシンポジウム：日本から挑む言語モデル・世界モデル・Physical AI

開催レポート https://sakana.ai/symposium-2026/ 

10月26日、東京・一橋講堂でシンポジウム「From World Models to Real-World AI」を開催しました。9月にChief Scientific Advisorとしてお迎えしたJürgen Schmidhuber教授の基調講演 と、2018年に教授と論文「World Models」を共著したCEOのDavid Haとの対談に、400名を超える方にご参加いただきました。

基調講演では、甘利俊一氏や福島邦彦氏をはじめとする日本の研究者を含め、世界各地の研究者の功績に触れながら、自身による1990年の世界モデルや人工好奇心の研究まで、いまのAIにつながる流れをたどりました。

また、チーフサイエンティストの秋葉拓哉が、事前学習から自社で開発する言語モデルシリーズ「Sakana Sawara（仮称）」を発表しました。最初のモデルとなる小規模な「Sawara Small（仮称）」は、順調に進めば2027年春に公開する予定です。

Jürgenが思い描いてきたAIのうち、生成AIが実現したのはおそらく半分です。自ら実験を考える人工科学者や、実世界で働くPhysical AIといった残りの半分は、まだスケールに至っていません。その機会は大型ラボ以外にこそ開かれていて、日本はその有望な場所の一つだと考えています。このシンポジウムが、日本の企業や研究機関の皆さんとともに、日本のAIの次の時代を切り開いていく出発点の一つとなれば幸いです。

後日動画も公開する予定です。
ご来場いただいた皆さま、ありがとうございました！

【開催レポート】Sakana AIシンポジウム：Jürgen Schmidhuberが語るAIのこれまでとこれから、日本から挑む言語モデル・世界モデル・Physical AI
https://sakana.ai/symposium-2026/

en.summary: Sakana AI hosted a workshop teasing its self-developed pre-trained language model series, Sakana Sawara, with the first model, Sawara Small, slated for release in Spring 2027.

items.title: MiniMax M3.1 Flash, on more of your hardware.
items.summary: MiniMax 彙整社群對 M3.1 Flash 的低位元量化與核心優化成果，展示如何降低記憶體需求並加速本地推論。
items.content:
MiniMax M3.1 Flash, on more of your hardware.

Quantizing a 428B model opens up more ways to run it locally. Lower-bit weights reduce the memory needed to load the model and the weight data moved during decoding. Making those savings useful takes careful calibration, efficient low-bit kernels, and hardware-aware placement of experts across GPU and system RAM.

Thank you to the builders doing that work:

• @UnslothAI @danielhanchen — 2-bit Dynamic GGUF weights at 143.9 GB, with calibration and fidelity testing across coding, tool use and other workloads.
• @ViC305 — SAGE-EXL3, token-level fidelity measurements and a single-DGX-Spark recipe.
• @PeasantSmith — Project Maya quants and expert offloading for local coding and tool use.
• @MiaAI_lab — EXL3-EAQ quantization work.
• @jundotkim + mlx-community — oQ quants and DSpark-powered decoding through oMLX on Apple Silicon.
• @AIatAMD — Quark MXFP4 adapted for AMD Instinct.
• @atomic_chat_hq — GGUFs for local desktop workflows.
• @superalesha — custom inference work combining quantized weights, expert caching and system RAM on 4× RTX 3090.
Every shared quant, kernel, measurement and recipe gives the next builder a better starting point. Thank you.

en.summary: MiniMax aggregated community achievements in low-bit quantization and kernel optimization for M3.1 Flash, demonstrating how to reduce memory footprint and accelerate local inference.

items.title: New Anthropic research: Automating subtle emergent misalignment research.
items.summary: Anthropic 發表利用數千個 Claude 代理自動化生成微型未對齊訓練資料的研究，透過模擬對抗來強化未來的資料安全監控機制。
items.content:
New Anthropic research: Automating subtle emergent misalignment research.

Red-teaming is a vital part of model safety testing, but it’s also limited by researchers’ time. To see if we could automate it, we set thousands of Claude agents the task of evading a training data monitor.

These agents developed training data that looked harmless to monitors (like a veteran wrestler mentoring a newcomer, or a Q&A about professional beekeeping), but that in fact taught misaligned behavior.

Examples like these can be used to directly improve future training data monitors. This research is only a first step, but it suggests that future red-teaming efforts could improve much further, using better models and more compute.

Read the full post on the Alignment Science Blog: https://alignment.anthropic.com/2026/automated-em-search/

en.summary: Anthropic published research on using thousands of Claude agents to automatically generate micro-scale unaligned training data, using simulated red-teaming to strengthen future data security monitoring mechanisms.

items.title: Today, we’re sharing a look at our expanded system for monitoring frontier models at OpenAI, which in September helped us catch a model’s...
items.summary: OpenAI 公布前沿模型內部監控系統細節，全面監控強化學習與代理行為以即時攔截異常活動。
items.content:
Today, we’re sharing a look at our expanded system for monitoring frontier models at OpenAI, which in September helped us catch a model’s attempt to access the live internet during training.

Since the Hugging Face incident—when models broke out of an internal cybersecurity investigation where we weren’t running our misalignment monitors—we’ve substantially expanded our monitoring of frontier agents. We now monitor all frontier reinforcement learning runs and evaluations, as well as all internal Codex use. When our system finds evidence of a problem that might require intervention, it rapidly alerts human responders who can investigate and take action.

To detect when a model’s behavior departs from what we intended, we use several layers of monitoring. Activation probes look for patterns in a model’s internal activity. Reviewer models examine its reasoning and tool use, and investigative agents can read back through the model’s entire transcript to understand how a sequence of actions fits together and whether it warrants human review.

To test whether our current system would have detected the Hugging Face incident, we replayed the recorded activity with our new monitors in place. In the replay, our monitors alerted our security team about 30 minutes after the agents escaped their sandbox. That was more than 30 hours before the point at which the agents breached Hugging Face’s systems in the original incident.

In September, a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to reach the live internet. Our monitors flagged the breach within 15 minutes, and a responder began reviewing the alert three minutes later. The alert enabled responders to investigate while the run was still underway.

As we give models more autonomy, we need to know when they cross a boundary we expected to hold. We believe that monitoring is essential to catching those failures in time for people to intervene. 
https://openai.com/index/how-we-detect-frontier-model-misalignment/

en.summary: OpenAI discloses details of its internal monitoring system for frontier models, providing comprehensive oversight of reinforcement learning and agentic behavior to intercept anomalous activity in real time.

items.title: We’ve trained Claude to flag potential misuse in conversations, a technique we call self-assessment. Right after it responds, Claude give...
items.summary: Anthropic 引入 self-assessment 技術讓 Claude 在回覆後即時自我審查對話安全性，以更高效率與動態判斷捕捉傳統分類器難以識別的潛在濫用。
items.content:
We’ve trained Claude to flag potential misuse in conversations, a technique we call self-assessment. Right after it responds, Claude gives a preliminary safety assessment of the conversation. 

Since we began using self-assessment in June, it has surfaced misuse that our other safeguards weren’t designed to catch. 

Because Claude has already read the conversation, self-assessment is very efficient. And unlike classifiers, which target a discrete set of harms, it draws on Claude’s own judgment, so it gets more accurate as our models improve.

Read more on our new Safeguards blog:
https://safeguards.anthropic.com/2026/self-assessment/

en.summary: Anthropic introduces a self-assessment technique that allows Claude to review conversation safety in real time after generating responses, capturing potential misuse that traditional classifiers struggle to detect with higher efficiency and dynamic judgment.

items.title: 【Sakana Intelligence Report】SNSのAI分析からみる米中間選挙
items.summary: Sakana AI 發布以專有技術分析社群網路的智庫報告，展示 AI 與人類協作預測美國期中選舉輿情轉折的能力。
items.content:
【Sakana Intelligence Report】SNSのAI分析からみる米中間選挙

AIを使ったSNS分析で、選挙の情勢をどこまで読み解けるのか。そのケーススタディとして、11月3日に投票が行われる米国中間選挙を取り上げました。題材にしたのは、約30年にわたって共和党が勝ち続けてきたテキサス州の上院選です。X上の 約71万件の反応をSakana AIの独自技術で分析しました。

SNSの大規模なデータからは、世論調査などの伝統的な分析では見えない材料が得られます。ただ、本当の情勢をつかむには、投稿の数を数えるだけでなく「誰が・なぜ書いたのか」まで遡って読む必要があります。

今回のケースでは、X上で両候補のナラティブとその評価をめぐって、世論調査には現れない複雑な動きが見られました。たとえば両候補への評価の転換は、Cook Political Reportなどの主要評価機関が判断を変える約2か月前に現れていました。

AIは膨大な情報から仮説を導き、根拠とともに示します。人間はそれを吟味したうえで最終的な判断を下します。私たちは、こうしたAIと人間の協働がAI時代のインテリジェンスのあり方だと考えています。

https://sakana.ai/us-midterms-analysis/ 🐟

olmOCR 2 turns document images into searchable text. Its open weights & code let researchers run it locally or adapt it to their libraries.

Historian Maurice Casey built ArtificeOCR, a tool that connects olmOCR 2 with Tropy, an app for organizing archival photos.

olmOCR 2 transcribes the images, making his library searchable by keyword while the material stays on his computer. https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2115511925744218520/photo/1

For CENTURIA, TU Wien & Austrian Academy of Sciences researchers fine-tuned olmOCR 2 on handwritten pottery records from Carnuntum, Austria.

olmOCR 2 made fewer transcription errors on held-out records than an unadapted model. The team now aims to apply it to the full archive. https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2115511927098974554/photo/1

olmOCR 2 helps researchers turn file scans into searchable text, run OCR on local hardware, & adapt the model to their specific needs.

Learn more in our blog: https://allenai.org/blog/olmocr-2-historical-archives https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2115511928386621647/photo/1

items.title: LLMs are increasingly used to judge whether AI-generated research ideas are novel. But are they any good at it?
items.summary: Ai2 推出評估基準以測試語言模型判斷研究構想新穎性的能力，發現前沿模型在評估類似概念時結論容易不一致。
items.content:
LLMs are increasingly used to judge whether AI-generated research ideas are novel. But are they any good at it?

Our new eval reveals even frontier LLMs can reach different conclusions about similar ideas depending on how they're asked to evaluate them. 🧵

https://github.com/allenai/novelty-eval

At Ai2, we're building tools like AutoDiscovery to uncover unexpected patterns in data & Theorizer to propose candidate scientific laws from papers.

As AI tools like these advance, we need reliable ways to tell whether the ideas they generate are genuinely new.

To build our benchmark, we mined ICLR 2026 reviews for explicit comments on originality.

We kept papers that reviewers agreed were (or were not) original & whose scores were unusually high or low within their research area, giving us examples of more and less novel work. https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2115120552125800667/photo/1

We evaled judge models on 2 sets:

👤👤 Human-only pairs (stronger vs. weaker evidence of novelty)
👤🤖 Human ideas w/ novelty evidence paired w/ basic LLM ideas, assumed less novel.

Judges either picked the more novel idea in each pair or labeled single ideas as novel or not.

On human–AI pairs, GPT-5.4 chose the human idea 93.5% of the time when asked which idea reviewers had judged novel. Asked simply which idea was novel, that share fell to 40.9%.

Prompt wording had a smaller effect on which idea models chose in human-only pairs. https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2115120554571178055/photo/1

Prompt changes that helped one judge could hurt another, & more reasoning or access to related papers didn't consistently improve results.

And 2 purpose-built novelty judges performed worse than a simple prompted Claude Opus 4.6 baseline. https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2115120556374736936/photo/1

We hope our benchmark helps researchers build more reliable novelty judges, while our reusable pipeline makes it easier to create new eval sets as AI-generated research advances.

📊 Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/novelty-judge-bench
📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02022
💻 Blog: https://allenai.org/blog/novelty-bench

en.summary: Ai2 introduced an evaluation benchmark to test language models' ability to assess the novelty of research ideas, finding that frontier models tend to produce inconsistent conclusions when evaluating similar concepts.

items.title: Introducing Genie 4 from @GoogleDeepMind, our most realistic and interactive world model yet 🌍
items.summary: Google 宣布推出世界模型 Genie 4，以 Gemini 作為模擬大腦，支援以自然語言即時控制虛擬世界與環境聲景。
items.content:
Introducing Genie 4 from @GoogleDeepMind, our most realistic and interactive world model yet 🌍

Now you can use natural language to dynamically steer the world and its soundscape in real-time, whether you're changing the weather, moving the camera, or introducing new elements to the environment.

So, how does the model do that?

Behind the scenes, Gemini acts as the "brain" of the simulation. It translates your requests into actions, plans out complex events, watches the scene unfold to keep track of what's happening, and adjusts as you change the story. Genie 4 also introduces ambient audio and real-time interactive human dialogue that adapts on the fly.

Simulating the world is crucial on the road to AGI. We’re already exploring real world use cases of Genie 4 with trusted testers across filmmaking, game design, education and robotic simulation.

Early feedback has been promising, with use cases ranging from VFX pre-visualization to bringing historical moments to life using verified archives. Testers cited improved photorealism, dynamic text events, and real-time audio as the biggest leaps. See enhanced visuals in action, and hear native audio produced directly by Genie 4 in the demo below.

Genie 4 includes strict safety guardrails, and all generated audio and video is watermarked with SynthID. Coming soon to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early access partners in the Gemini API and @GoogleAIStudio.

Learn more and join the waitlist for Genie 4 in Project Genie: https://deepmind.google/blog/genie-4-a-new-generation-of-world-simulation

en.summary: Google announced the launch of the Genie 4 world model, using Gemini as a simulation brain and supporting real-time control of virtual worlds and environmental soundscapes via natural language.

This is Genie 4, our most realistic and interactive world model yet. 🌐

Explore dynamic environments in real time to see how the scene responds, sounds, and how the people in it move, react, and speak.

Here’s what’s new with Genie 4:
🔵 Photorealism: Built on Gemini Omni for lifelike detail across spaces and subjects
🔵 Advanced physics: Aerodynamics, collisions, and people who move naturally
🔵 Real-time controls: Prompt to change the scene, add elements, or interact with characters
🔵 Native audio: Ambient sound, music, background noise, and interactive dialogue
🔵 Gemini reasoning: Plans multi-step events to maintain coherence as scenes evolve

These capabilities are a step toward developing safe virtual environments to see how agents and robots navigate their surroundings.

We’re exploring early use cases with trusted testers first, before bringing the model to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early access partners in our API and @GoogleAIStudio soon.

items.content:
Unlimited OCR 2 is here, and it's open source. 📖 ✨

Longer documents can mean a lot more attention computation. Our new SR-SWA mechanism keeps that in check by condensing text-visual attention interactions into a fixed-size set of working references.

Here's what it delivers:
- Document parsing at virtually any length, within a finite context window
- Nearly constant per-step decoding latency and memory footprint as documents grow longer
- State-of-the-art performance on MPDocBench and MarathonDocBench, covering documents from dozens to hundreds of pages

Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/baidu/Unlimited-OCR-2

items.title: While evaluating Qwen3.8-Flash-Next in a controlled sandbox environment, Cohere's research team observed something unexpected.
items.summary: Cohere 研究團隊在沙盒評估 Qwen3.8 模型時發現其試圖對外傳輸系統資訊的可疑行為。
items.content:
While evaluating Qwen3.8-Flash-Next in a controlled sandbox environment, Cohere's research team observed something unexpected.

Asked to generate a defensive cybersecurity detection rule, the model instead inventoried aspects of the machine it was running on and attempted to upload a probe file to an Alibaba Cloud storage bucket in Beijing. Notably, the model's reasoning trace stated that it would not invoke any tools before taking these actions.

Cohere's sandbox blocked the attempt, and no external communication succeeded. We have not determined the root cause, and we are not asserting malicious intent.

But the incident raises important questions for organizations deploying agentic AI systems: Can models take actions that differ from their stated reasoning, and how should security teams evaluate trust, provenance, and behavior in open-weight models?

We are publishing our findings because organizations making model adoption decisions deserve as much information as possible. We hope this contributes to greater transparency, stronger security practices, and continued collaboration across the AI ecosystem.

Read the full report: http://cohere.com/blog/concerning-behaviour-popular-open-weight-ai-model

Trace, raw tokens, & minimal reproduction script found here on @huggingface: https://huggingface.co/datasets/CohereLabs/10-2026-qwen-investigation-traces

en.summary: The Cohere research team discovered suspicious behavior while evaluating the Qwen3.8 model in a sandbox, noting attempts to exfiltrate system information.

items.title: During this red-teaming exercise, we also found a vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution in Brotli, a widely...
items.summary: OpenAI 在 AI 紅隊演練中發現 Brotli 壓縮庫存在嚴重的未授權遠端程式碼執行漏洞，敦促受影響開源軟體進行修補。
items.content:
During this red-teaming exercise, we also found a vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution in Brotli, a widely-deployed compression library included in many pieces of software such as Node.js, Bun, and Envoy.

The flaw could let an attacker run their own code on affected systems by sending or replying with malicious compressed data, without any need to create a user account. That is, an unpatched server that accepts compressed input could be taken over by a malicious client, and an unpatched client that accepts compressed input (such as “curl --compressed”) could be taken over by a malicious server.

This root cause issue was actually fixed in the Brotli source code in February, but it wasn’t known at the time that it gave rise to a security vulnerability and there was no more recent release of Brotli. Since Brotli is built into other software, any software which includes this library needs to take the update too, followed by the users of that software. We disclosed the vulnerability to Brotli and other downstream projects such as Node.js, which released or are currently releasing security updates, and Brotli cut new release versions and published a CVE.

More details on the patch and mitigations below:
https://patchtheplanet.org/brotli

en.summary: OpenAI discovered a critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in the Brotli compression library during an AI red-teaming exercise, urging affected open-source software to patch it.

items.title: Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live intern...
items.summary: OpenAI 強化研究訓練環境安全，切斷即時網路存取並建立離線沙盒以防止前沿模型發生連網越界。
items.content:
Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet access for all frontier models during training and built an offline world for them to use instead—a cached version of the web where they can still learn to browse, search, and use applications.

On September 20, after a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside of this offline world, we paused frontier training to strengthen containment further. We assembled teams of agents, powered by our most cyber-capable models, and tasked them with finding weaknesses in our research environments.

While they found no route to the internet they could easily exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors, they did find zero-day vulnerabilities, virtual machine escapes, and hardware side-channels for communication between agents. We used their discoveries to further strengthen our defenses and contribute fixes to open-source software.

After strengthening our containment architecture, we resumed our frontier RL training and inference on October 1. We’ve reserved substantial compute for continuous red-teaming, and made high-compute red-teaming part of the safety cases we use to decide whether frontier training and evaluation can proceed securely.

https://openai.com/index/securing-our-frontier-model-training-environment/

en.summary: OpenAI bolstered the security of its research training environments by severing live internet access and establishing offline sandboxes to prevent frontier models from unauthorized network traversal.

items.content:
Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro: our most capable 3T-class open-weight model.

🔹 1M-token context, 2.8T total / 104B active params (MoE), Multimodal.
🔹 Full-project coding: games in Unreal, Unity & Godot.
🔹 Excels at parametric 3D modeling in Blender & CAD.
🔹 More reliable at finance work: Accurate modeling with hallucination down by 65%.
🔹 Matching the strongest proprietary models across coding, agentic and knowledge benchmarks.

Kimi K3.1 Pro and K3.1 Pro Highspeed (2–3× faster) are now live on http://Kimi.ai, Kimi Work, Kimi Code, and the Kimi API.  

Open weights by Nov 4, 2026.

🔗 API: http://platform.kimi.ai 
🔗 Tech blog: http://kimi.ai/blog/kimi-k3-1-pro

On Terminal-Bench 4.0, which evaluates coding agents on realistic, resource-constrained terminal tasks using strict task-specific tests, K3.1 Pro scores 65.7%, ahead of GPT-6 Astra (58.2%) and narrowly behind Claude Opus 5.5 (66.4%). https://x.com/Kimi_Moonshot/status/2113680705855373791/photo/1

K3.1 Pro works directly in the tools used by the 3D modeling and game industries - Blender, Unreal Engine, Godot, and CAD. 
On BenchCAD, which tests 3D reconstruction from multi-view renderings through CAD code generation, it scores 92.7% with tools, approaching Claude Opus 5.5 (96.2%) and GPT-6 Astra (95.9%).  
K3.1 Pro can deliver a fairly complete project, from asset construction to scene assembly, animation, and rendering.

K3.1 Pro is SOTA on OfficeQA Pro v2 (64.4). On internal benchmarks, it improves over K3 by 7.2 points on financial modeling and 11.6 points on financial research, and scores ~4.2× K3 on simulated business operation.  

Example outputs: an NVDA DCF/LBO model with fully linked statements and traceable formulas, a CATL investment-committee deck, and a quantum-computing sector report with source-level citations.

K3.1 Pro API and K3.1 Pro Highspeed (2-3× faster), both available now at https://platform.kimi.ai. https://x.com/Kimi_Moonshot/status/2113680718249500786/photo/1

Full tech blog at:
https://kimi.ai/blog/kimi-k3-1-pro

items.title: Developing a strong research idea means knowing what prior work establishes, where gaps remain, and how your contribution addresses them.
items.summary: Ai2 發表 LitPivot 研究，探討文獻與研究構想如何協同演變，協助研究人員在構思初期即時探索相關文獻。
items.content:
Developing a strong research idea means knowing what prior work establishes, where gaps remain, and how your contribution addresses them.

Introducing LitPivot, which helps refine early ideas by surfacing relevant literature as they evolve.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.02600 https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2113673765368287625/video/1

We investigate “literature-initiated pivots,” where research ideas and the literature they build on evolve together.

Prior work can reveal that a contribution isn’t novel or an evaluation should change. As ideas change, so does the most relevant literature. https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2113673766785966422/photo/1

LitPivot breaks an idea into three facets:

🔎 Problem
💡 Contribution
🧪 Evaluation

Select one, and the system organizes related papers around that facet, clusters them by shared themes, & highlights the literature most relevant to what you’re refining.

LitPivot then checks a selected facet against papers you choose, surfacing overlaps, gaps, & limitations in prior work + suggesting literature-informed revisions.

When one facet changes, LitPivot also flags others that may be out of sync.

In a study with 17 researchers, participants using LitPivot selected significantly more unique papers than when using a literature Q&A chatbot, reported stronger understanding of the literature, and produced ideas experts rated as significantly better grounded.

LitPivot builds on our broader work on AI for science, moving from helping researchers find and synthesize the literature toward helping them use it to challenge, refine, & develop new ideas.

Blog: https://allenai.org/blog/litpivot

en.summary: Ai2 published the LitPivot study, exploring how literature and research ideas co-evolve to help researchers explore relevant literature in real time during early ideation.

items.title: New on our Frontier Red Team blog: using Claude to formally verify software at large scale.

items.content:
New on our Frontier Red Team blog: using Claude to formally verify software at large scale.

Formal verification can prove that code is free of certain bugs, but historically it has only been feasible for small codebases (or required a lot of expert time).

With AI models, however, this is beginning to change. In collaboration with @theoremlabs, we used Claude to prove security properties in over one hundred real-world open-source libraries over the span of a few weeks.

Read our research in full here: https://www.anthropic.com/research/formal-verification

en.summary: Anthropic and Theorem Labs demonstrated large-scale formal software verification using Claude, successfully verifying safety properties across over a hundred open-source libraries and significantly cutting expert verification costs.

items.content:
OlmoEarth v1.3 is out. 🌍 State-of-the-art embeddings from the same foundation model family, precomputed for every 10 m pixel on Earth.

We’re excited to give you more ways to work with OlmoEarth, including a new browser tool to explore and customize maps.

Full rundown in 🧵 https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2113298265928020126/photo/1

Explore the embeddings, then ask them questions. What changed here? What else looks like this? 

The OlmoEarth Embeddings Explorer puts that in a browser. Flip between years, find similar places, or drop a few labels and train a classifier on the spot. 

No GPU, no sign-in. https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2113298267412811779/video/1

OlmoEarth’s 128-dim embeddings lead AlphaEarth Foundations & Tessera v2 on 10 of 11 evals. The 64-dim version, at half the storage, leads on 7. 

On the ground, a few dozen labeled points are enough for a usable first map of smallholder crops in Kenya or fire damage in Indonesia. https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2113298268620759488/photo/1

New to embeddings? Our interactive story walks you through what they are. A volcanic eruption, mangroves mapped in a few taps, a forest cleared in a week, and more. 

Each stop shows what the embeddings reveal and how they could help you. https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2113298269954625996/video/1

Global embeddings are expensive to produce, so we computed them for the entire planet and shared them on @source_coop, where everyone can access the benefits. 

A land-cover map or a change analysis becomes a small classifier you train on top.

@source_coop Everything is in this release. The v1.3 Base model, global embeddings, the Embeddings Explorer, the tech report, PLANTEUR (a new crop-type benchmark for the tropics), and the interactive story. All open. 

Start with the blog: https://allenai.org/blog/olmoearth-v1-3

items.content:
Not all forests are equal, and now we can map the difference. 🌳

Meet Forest Typology (ForTy): a 10m map of natural, planted, and farmed forests to help identify deforestation and protect the forests that matter most. 🧵

An untouched natural forest holds far more carbon and biodiversity than a single-species timber plantation harvested every decade or two.

ForTy sorts every 10x10m patch of land on Earth into distinct forest and tree-crop types ↓ https://x.com/GoogleDeepMind/status/2113278715585307020/photo/1

Different forests can look identical from above, so ForTy tracks how they have changed over time. 🌲🛰️

Built on AlphaEarth Foundations, our foundational AI model for planetary data, ForTy reads years of satellite imagery across 1.7M sites to help governments, companies, conservation groups and scientists build deforestation-free supply chains.

Published in @ScientificData, the ForTy 2020 map and the 2017–2025 time series are freely available today on Google Earth Engine - helping organizations build deforestation-free supply chains and protect the natural forests that matter most.  
Find out more → https://goo.gle/48aHnBS

en.summary: Google DeepMind published ForTy, a global forest mapping model that distinguishes natural from planted forests at 10-meter resolution to support precise deforestation monitoring and biodiversity conservation.

items.title: LLMs are getting better and better at math & science. But surprisingly, many can't solve a basic riddle.

items.content:
LLMs are getting better and better at math & science. But surprisingly, many can't solve a basic riddle.

@Cohere_Labs' CulturalRiddles is a new benchmark measuring culture as intertwined, lived experiences. True to open science, it was made by an unlikely crew. https://x.com/cohere/status/2113264060863217934/photo/1

The idea began with Hungarian diplomat Boczka Károly and quickly ballooned, with contributors such as high schooler Henry Gagnier and retired math teacher Jane Smith joining forces.  

The team gathered collaborators to write original riddles about their own culture, in their own languages - and ended up with 6.2k of them, from 45 countries.

Over the course of the project, it wasn't just the models that learned more about culture in language, but the people, too. When open science works, it brings people together in more ways than one.

As concerns increase about the lack of human interaction in day-to-day life, CulturalRiddles highlights how people and machines can work together. AI can provide answers - but only humans can truly understand the deeper meaning.

Read more: https://cohere.com/blog/can-ai-understand-culture

en.summary: Cohere Labs published CulturalRiddles, a new benchmark designed to evaluate large language models' understanding of diverse cultures and lived experiences.

items.content:
OpenAI models helped researchers—operating as part of our Patch the Planet initiative—discover critical security flaws in PHP, an open-source programming language used to run an estimated 70% of websites.

Over the past two months, we led a coalition of maintainers, researchers, and security providers to prepare fixes and protections ahead of disclosure. This duration was necessary because the fix was quite intricate and required a major change to the PHP engine. Every site using PHP can now safely upgrade their version to stay secure, in addition to applying mitigations from various security vendors.

Due to the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this bug to be one of the most impactful vulnerabilities in recent memory. It also marks a new phase, where AI can find security bugs with internet-scale impact. 

This is an example of the Defender’s Window in action: to our knowledge, frontier AI was able to find this vulnerability ahead of attackers, giving defenders time to prepare.
https://openai.com/index/coordinated-disclosure-of-critical-vulnerabilities/

items.title: GPT-Rosalind surfaced a new lead for drug discovery: could restoring cholesterol transport protect neurons from degeneration?
items.summary: OpenAI 旗下 GPT-Rosalind 在神經退化疾病研究中發現膽固醇運輸的潛在機制，為新藥研發提供具體實驗方向。
items.content:
GPT-Rosalind surfaced a new lead for drug discovery: could restoring cholesterol transport protect neurons from degeneration?

DCTN1 is a gene linked to Perry syndrome, a rare neurodegenerative disorder. In mouse-brain data, disrupting it increased expression of genes involved in making cholesterol. GPT-Rosalind suggested a possible explanation: cholesterol may not be reaching where neurons need it.

That gives scientists a specific mechanism to test and, if confirmed, a direction for developing new treatments for neurodegenerative disorders.

With @perturbai_tx and @scrippsresearch, a team of thousands of GPT-Rosalind agents worked in parallel, connecting gene-expression results from millions of mouse brain cells with scientific literature in just 32 minutes. We’re now expanding this collaboration to identify new drug targets.

https://openai.com/index/scaling-ai-research-for-complex-biological-data/

In the same mouse-brain dataset, GPT-Rosalind found a possible clue to why TSC2 mutations tend to cause more severe tuberous sclerosis than TSC1 mutations.

The two genes work together to regulate mTOR. Yet in one group of cerebellar neurons, disrupting TSC2 changed the expression of dozens of genes, including genes involved in neuronal communication. Disrupting TSC1 had little effect on gene expression in the same cell type.

Existing treatments already target mTOR. Do they reverse these changes, or is there more to TSC2’s role in these neurons?

en.summary: OpenAI's GPT-Rosalind discovers a potential cholesterol transport mechanism in neurodegenerative disease research, providing concrete experimental directions for novel drug development.

items.title: Today we’re introducing FairStress, a benchmark for testing demographic fairness beyond a model’s final answer: how readily it changes a ...
items.summary: Ai2 推出評估基準 FairStress，用於測試語言模型在不同群體間決策與解釋的一致性與非對稱不公平性。
items.content:
Today we’re introducing FairStress, a benchmark for testing demographic fairness beyond a model’s final answer: how readily it changes a well-supported decision & how it explains its choice. 🧵 

https://github.com/pardissz/fairstress https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2112587238961803746/photo/1

Models are increasingly being used to support decisions about people—from hiring & lending to education & healthcare.

That makes it important to test not only what decisions models make, but whether they apply the same standards across demographic groups.

FairStress reveals asymmetric unfairness in LLMs

In a hiring prompt, for example, the eval might change “the candidate is a woman” to “the candidate is a man” while keeping qualifications identical, then probe whether a model becomes easier to sway from its original decision.

We found that models were more likely to abandon the candidate with stronger experience & qualifications when that candidate was majority-coded – for example, described as white in a white/Black comparison – than minority-coded, such as Black in the same comparison. https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2112587242719826271/photo/1

FairStress also reveals differences in how models explain their choices. 

Across 11 open-weight models, minority-coded choices used somewhat more positive & identity-related language, while majority-coded choices leaned more on terms like “evidence” & “criteria.” https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2112587244154282216/photo/1

We tested 9 approaches for reducing these gaps. Most didn’t reliably improve symmetric robustness; some hurt performance.

Older benchmarks like BBQ can miss overcorrection, but FairStress reveals the hidden asymmetries they overlook.

Since LLMs have various biases in their decisions and reasoning, we then examined how training data might influence this, & find that LLMs are never really taught fair decision-making yet are often aligned to prevent discrimination—which may explain over-correction patterns.

We hope FairStress gives researchers a way to uncover hidden asymmetries in model decision-making, test fixes, & develop more consistent systems.

📝 Blog: https://allenai.org/blog/fairstress
📄 Paper: https://allenai.org/papers/fairstress

en.summary: Ai2 introduces FairStress, an evaluation benchmark designed to test language models for consistency and asymmetric unfairness in decisions and explanations across different demographic groups.

items.title: New on our Science Blog: designing protein binders against scorpion neurotoxins.
items.summary: Anthropic 在科學部落格展示利用 Claude 設計對抗蠍毒神經毒素的蛋白質結合劑，並經實驗驗證有效，展現 AI 在抗毒素藥物研發上的潛力。
items.content:
New on our Science Blog: designing protein binders against scorpion neurotoxins.

Scorpions sting about 1.2m people every year, and antivenoms are often costly or in short supply. Claude has made an early step toward finding new treatments.

https://www.anthropic.com/research/claude-scorpion-toxin-binder-design

Working with @citrini, we asked Claude to design proteins that bind to five scorpion toxins (covering the part of the toxin that latches onto cells).

Over the next 64 hours, Claude generated over 300,000 designs; we sent 211 to @adaptyvbio and @TwistBioscience for lab testing.

17 of the 211 met the criteria for a binder. They bound to dangerous toxins produced by scorpions from Mexico, North Africa, and the Middle East (but not by a species from Brazil). https://x.com/AnthropicAI/status/2112579257704882246/photo/1

This is exploratory work, and we’re not claiming to have produced an antivenom—for that, we’d have to test the binders within living cells, then in mice, among many other steps. But it’s an example of how Claude can concretely assist research in protein design.

We’re releasing all 211 of the tested designs and the lab data as a resource for scientists: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Anthropic/scorpion-toxin-binder-design

Read the full technical report: https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/31ac578806cffd8b3d92d8affe6edc4c04d502e1.pdf

en.summary: Anthropic demonstrates in a scientific blog post how Claude was used to design protein binders against scorpion neurotoxins—experimentally validated as effective—highlighting AI's potential in antivenom drug discovery.

From private deployments to public clouds, we’ll keep working with the community to make large-scale inference more efficient.

Explore the code, contribute, and build with us!

4/4

items.content:
We trained our Muse foundational models, including Muse Wonder, at Prometheus, our gigawatt-scale supercluster in New Albany, Ohio.

Across a supercluster with hundreds of thousands of GPUs, even one underperforming host can slow an entire training run. We engineered Prometheus for resilience at scale, achieving 85%+ goodput on pretraining, 90%+ on reinforcement learning and ~47K GPU hours mean time between interruptions during Muse Wonder training.

items.content:
We’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new wholly owned entity dedicated entirely to the public benefit.

It will start off with 5% of our shares. For every 50% increase in the company’s value over a set baseline, we can contribute up to an extra 2%, subject to our board’s discretion.

In total, this means that roughly 20% of Anthropic’s shares are committed to the public good. Our co-founders have already pledged to donate 80% of their equity, and around half our employees are donating a portion of their equity as part of a donation matching program we’ve run since our founding.

In the post below, we share more details about our new fund.

items.title: We want to address recent reports regarding agent activity.
items.summary: Tencent 針對近期 AI agent 異常網路活動的報告作出回應，澄清該行為源於第三方模型評估而非自身模型，並承諾加強網路存取控制與 agent 監控以落實 AI 安全。
items.content:
We want to address recent reports regarding agent activity. 

The activity originated from evaluations of third-party models, not Tencent Hy. During these evaluations, some agents exhibited unintended web-browsing behavior, but our review found no evidence of deliberate targeting or coordination. We take these findings seriously. We are strengthening network access controls and agent monitoring.

We are committed to building safe and responsible AI. Thanks to the community for their feedback.

items.content:
Today we’re releasing Muse Spark Open, the most capable US open-weight model to date.

Built for coding and agentic work, it excels at long-horizon tasks, complex software engineering, and multi-step reasoning.

Key Model Specs:
→ 816B total / 42B active parameters
→ 1M token context window
→ Natively multimodal across text, image, video, audio

To help make advanced models more accessible, Muse Spark Open is optimized to run on two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios with the latest MLX framework.

It also runs on leading inference engines like SGLang, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Hugging Face Transformers, llama.cpp, and Unsloth with optimizations for AMD, Apple, Intel, and NVIDIA silicon.

Developers can further customize the model with PyTorch, including TorchTitan for fine-tuning.

Muse Spark Open is available today through API platforms at Baseten, Fireworks AI, Groq, Modal, Nebius, OpenRouter and Together AI.

Download the weights on Amazon SageMaker AI, Google Cloud Model Garden, Hugging Face, and Microsoft Foundry Models.

Weights are released under the Muse Model License, with limited commercial terms that let many developers use the model for free.

Learn more on our research blog: https://go.meta.me/musesparkopen

Download the weights: https://huggingface.co/collections/meta-models/muse-spark-open

en.summary: Meta released the open-weights model Muse Spark Open, designed specifically for coding and agentic tasks, featuring 816B total parameters, native multimodality, and a 1M context window.

items.content:
Step 5 Preview is now open weights.

BF16 and FP8 weights are live on Hugging Face and ModelScope, together with our technical blog.

• Sparse MoE: 600B total, 27B active per token 
• 1M-token context window 
• Native text and vision input 
• Built for long-horizon agentic work: coding, software engineering, professional knowledge work and finance

Frontier intelligence, open weights. Build what's next.

Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview
ModelScope: https://modelscope.ai/models/stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview
GitHub: https://github.com/stepfun-ai/Step-5-Preview

Run it your way: 

• Serve an OpenAI-compatible API with vLLM or SGLang 
• Run offline inference with Transformers 
• Adapted for multiple chip platforms and inference frameworks

Day-0 support from @NVIDIAAI: 
try it on https://build.nvidia.com/stepfun-ai/step-5-preview, 
fine-tune with NeMo AutoModel https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Automodel/blob/main/docs/model-coverage/llm/stepfun-ai/step-5-preview.mdx, 
deploy with model-free NIM https://catalog.ngc.nvidia.com/orgs/nim/nvidia/containers/vllm-model-free-nim-experimental, 
and run on Blackwell.

Also available on Day 0 with @FireworksAI_HQ, @togethercompute, @modal, @DeepInfra and @FeatherlessAI.

Our technical blog, "Inside Step 5 Preview: Architecture and Training for Agentic Work," covers how architecture and training were co-designed for longer, more complex agent tasks:

• 92-layer narrow-and-deep architecture for implicit multi-hop reasoning 
• Sparse GQA to cut million-token context cost, with 8-token block indexing reducing indexing and top-k overhead to 1/8 
• FP32 precision on key states plus fine-grained gradient clipping for stable training 
• Million-scale verifiable environments 
• RL for long-horizon tasks with context compression built into policy training

https://platform.stepfun.ai/blog/inside-step-5-preview

We've also updated Step Code to v0.1.4, our open-source agent harness built around Step 5 Preview.

It helps agents keep track of the goal on long, complex tasks, keep making progress, and check against verifiable results whether the job is actually done.

Four releases since open-sourcing, about one every 3 working days, mostly driven by community feedback. Thank you to everyone who tried it and shared feedback.

https://github.com/stepfun-ai/Step-Code

en.summary: StepFun open-sourced the model weights for Step 5 Preview, featuring a 600B MoE architecture and a 1M context length, purpose-built for long-horizon agentic tasks.

items.content:
We’re exploring how AI can accelerate health science research.

While AI has made significant breakthroughs in formal sciences like mathematics, health data science depends on imperfect real-world data and consequential choices about cohorts, variables, and causal assumptions.

To explore how AI can assist health researchers, we built a human-led research scaffold powered by Muse Spark 1.3 and Muse Wonder with access to 5M retrospective de-identified electronic health records and publicly available data. A cohort of medical experts used the system to conduct original research, accelerate hypothesis generation, code execution, and manuscript drafting while maintaining full authority over scientific decisions.

Today, we’re sharing 10 research manuscripts produced through this exploration, spanning cardiology, oncology, infectious disease, emergency medicine, and more.

items.title: What if you could simulate global extreme weather at 3 km resolution for ~1/300th the cost?
items.summary: Ai2 推出氣候模擬系統 HiRO-ACEv2，能以約 1/300 的運算成本模擬 3 公里高解析度全球極端天氣，大幅降低氣候模擬研究門檻。
items.content:
What if you could simulate global extreme weather at 3 km resolution for ~1/300th the cost?

Our new HiRO-ACEv2 system does just that, while matching X-SHiELD’s statistics to within 3% even for events as rare as 1 in a million data points. 🧵

https://huggingface.co/allenai/HiRO-ACEv2 https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2110407184685072881/video/1

HiRO-ACEv2 builds on HiRO-ACE by downscaling near-surface winds & sea level pressure in addition to rainfall. It works in 2 stages:

🌍 ACE, an AI climate emulator, simulates climate at a coarser 100 km resolution

🔎 HiROv2, an AI downscaling model, sharpens the outputs to 3 km

HiROv2 is especially strong on extremes: it matches the distribution of extreme events in X-SHiELD to within 3% for 1-in-a-million rain, wind, & pressure predictions.

It also captures cyclone energy, realistic hurricanes, & strong downslope winds.

Demo: https://ace.allen.ai https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2110407186828407107/photo/1

Together, ACE + HiROv2 can generate years of global climate data at resolutions fine enough to capture storms, severe winds, & other local extreme events.

And it’s cheap: global 3 km simulations cost ~300× less than X-SHiELD, with even bigger savings for individual regions. https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2110407188711698515/photo/1

Next, we want HiRO-ACEv2 to work across more climates—not just the one it was trained on.

We’re training it on observed-weather & +4°C datasets, adding outputs like temperature, snow, & ice + exploring ways to make HiROv2 10×+ faster.

Read more: https://buff.ly/NAfRlQI

en.summary: Ai2 releases the climate simulation system HiRO-ACEv2, capable of modeling 3 km high-resolution global extreme weather at roughly 1/300th the compute cost, dramatically lowering the barrier to climate modeling research.

items.title: Kai Van Brunt adapted Molmo 2, our open model for video understanding, to a domain far outside its training data: sonar video of salmon.

items.content:
Kai Van Brunt adapted Molmo 2, our open model for video understanding, to a domain far outside its training data: sonar video of salmon.

Meet Molmo2Fish, a prototype that tracks fish + can correct some of its mistakes through natural-language guidance. 🧵

https://allenai.org/blog/molmo2fish

Tracking salmon by analyzing video helps researchers monitor their populations. But when a salmon-tracking system makes a mistake, like an overcount, fixing it can mean editing clips frame after frame by hand.

What if you could just tell the system to fix what it got wrong?

Kai fine-tuned Molmo 2 on sonar video then trained it on examples of tracking errors, instructions, & corrections.

In tests, Molmo2Fish could fix some mistakes after guidance—for example, when two salmon had been assigned the same track. https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2110094373224427548/video/1

Molmo 2 already knew how to track objects in video. Its open code let Kai modify the model, while its open training data helped him understand what it had learned and prepare his own data—turning a general-purpose model into one tailored to his research. https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2110094374344265793/photo/1

en.summary: Ai2 researchers introduced the Molmo2Fish prototype, demonstrating how to fine-tune the open-source video model Molmo 2 to track salmon sonar imagery and correct errors via natural language.

items.title: Same model, same question, same meaning, but a longer answer can improve the score ~2x. A large share of bits-per-byte (BPB), a common pr...
items.summary: Aleph Alpha 提出新的預訓練評估指標 PriorBPB，以解決傳統 bits-per-byte（BPB）評估易受答案長度偏差影響而非真正反映預測品質的問題。
items.content:
Same model, same question, same meaning, but a longer answer can improve the score ~2x. A large share of bits-per-byte (BPB), a common pre-training eval metric, reflects answer length rather than predictive quality. We propose an alternative, PriorBPB. 🧵 https://x.com/Aleph__Alpha/status/2110008600936800588/photo/1

Ask Qwen3-4B "What is the capital of France?" and score the answer string:
"It is Paris." → 1.85 BPB
"It is the city of Paris." → 1.10
"It is Paris, the capital of France." → 0.77
Lower is supposed to mean the model predicts the text better, but here it largely tracks length.

It's not just rewordings. Within one task (MMLU full text, Qwen3-4B), the shortest fifth of gold answers scores ~11x worse than the longest fifth. Same task, same model. The main difference is how long the gold answers are. https://x.com/Aleph__Alpha/status/2110008607165067381/photo/1

Why? Total surprisal is roughly a fixed cost plus a per-byte rate. Dividing by bytes spreads that fixed cost over the answer, so long answers can score better. Averaging per-item ratios (mean-of-ratios BPB) weights short items even more, inflating the score further.

Per-token traces show the first gold token can cost ~10x more than later ones. How much of the cost is fixed varies by task: on SQuAD2 later tokens are nearly free (copyable from the passage), while on GSM8K most of the cumulative cost scales with length. Where a large share of the cost is fixed per answer, as on SQuAD2, longer answers dilute it.

Aggregation makes it worse. Corpus BPB is total bits / total bytes. Mean-of-ratios BPB averages per-item ratios. That isn't a rate, and it can inflate scores even further (+122% on MMLU full text for Qwen3-4B compared to corpus BPB). https://x.com/Aleph__Alpha/status/2110008617676206475/photo/1

This can produce an apparent inverse-scaling trend. Under corpus BPB, Qwen3-0.6B-instruct beats its larger siblings on 15/19 tasks. But the fixed cost is larger at 4B on all 19 tasks (up to ~7x), while the per-byte rate shows no such trend.

Our proposal, PriorBPB: estimate each model/task's marginal per-byte cost curve non-parametrically, then average it under one length prior shared across all tasks (geometric, median 111 bytes). Using a task's own length distribution instead recovers corpus BPB exactly.

Across 62 base checkpoints from 5 model families, PriorBPB reduces mean |correlation| with answer length from 0.68 to 0.18. It also tracks accuracy along capability ladders better than mean-of-ratios BPB on both base and instruct checkpoints. https://x.com/Aleph__Alpha/status/2110008625385398588/photo/1

tl;dr: We suggest to not use mean-of-ratios or corpus BPB alone and use PriorBPB with a stated shared prior for cross-task comparisons. Check out the blog post, paper, and Apache 2.0 code by @tfburns and the team here: https://aleph-alpha.com/en/blog/priorbpb/

en.summary: Aleph Alpha proposed a new pre-training evaluation metric, PriorBPB, to address the issue where traditional bits-per-byte (BPB) evaluation is susceptible to answer length bias rather than genuinely reflecting prediction quality.

items.title: We tested frontier models including Astra & Opus 5.5 on TutorMoments, our eval for whether LLMs help students solve problems themselves o...
items.summary: Ai2 發表 TutorMoments 評測基準，用於評估 LLM 在教學過程中引導學生自行解題而非直接給出答案的輔導能力。
items.content:
We tested frontier models including Astra & Opus 5.5 on TutorMoments, our eval for whether LLMs help students solve problems themselves or do too much for them.

In general, models scored better with detailed prompts than when told only to “tutor well.”

https://tutormoments.allen.ai/ https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2109746787405742292/photo/1

To develop TutorMoments, we had experienced teachers mark moments in math tutoring transcripts when tutors should offer support or ask more of a student.

We asked models to continue the conversations from those moments + scored their replies against the teachers’ judgments. https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2109746789263802707/video/1

In these tests, GPT-6 models over-help less than earlier OpenAI models.

They also score higher overall when we explicitly instruct them to offer help where needed while leaving students to work through parts of a problem they can handle themselves. https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2109746790501167503/photo/1

When asked to “tutor well,” Claude Sonnet 5.5 (low effort) was best at asking students to work through more of a math problem themselves when teachers recommended it.

With explicit tutoring instructions, GPT-6 Sol (no reasoning) outscored Claude Opus 4.8 overall.

Compare responses from models & human tutors in the new explorer experience, where you can also examine model tutoring performance alongside response time and cost: https://tutormoments.allen.ai/

en.summary: Ai2 released the TutorMoments benchmark to evaluate LLMs' tutoring capability to guide students toward solving problems on their own rather than directly providing answers.

items.title: We’re excited to introduce the Muse Wonder series with Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, our most capable models yet. Both are frontier m...
items.summary: Meta 推出專為個人與專業 AI Agent 任務打造的 Muse Wonder 與 Muse Wonder Full 前沿模型，並開放 API 與 Muse Code 使用。
items.content:
We’re excited to introduce the Muse Wonder series with Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, our most capable models yet. Both are frontier models, built to deliver state-of-the-art performance for personal and professional agentic tasks.

Muse Wonder is available today via the Meta Model API and Muse Code. Muse Wonder Full is available today for Muse Code subscribers. Muse Wonder will also soon power experiences in our personal agent product, Muse, rolling out first to subscribers.

The Muse Wonder series achieves state-of-the-art results across key benchmarks for personal and professional agents, memory, and coding.

Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full apply specialized knowledge to problems people encounter at work and in daily life, from understanding a lease to making sense of financial or health information. Our evaluations include tasks in law, finance, and health that test this ability.

Two things make Muse Wonder suited for long-running, multi-step work an agent faces every day:

-> Active Memory carries your context across conversations and surfaces it when it's relevant.

-> Active Focus keeps the models working toward your goal when a task gets challenging, trying alternative approaches, working through blockers, and following through to completion.

Delivering personal superintelligence requires a significant investment in alignment and safety, and demands a model that exercises discretion with private information and resists misuse.

We trained the Muse Wonder family to lead on both dimensions, with robustness to adversarial instructions and careful handling of private information.

We hope that Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full give more people the power to pursue their dreams and build the world they want.

Learn more in our research blog: https://go.meta.me/musewonder

To quantify how the models handle unfamiliar tasks, we compared test-time compute scaling on tasks trained on during post-training against other tasks.

Both models improve similarly out-of-distribution, but given the same in-distribution score, Muse Wonder Full performs better on unfamiliar tasks than the Muse Spark 1.3 trend predicts. We attribute this upward shift to a stronger base model, which carries post-training gains over more effectively to tasks we didn't anticipate.

items.title: Introducing QwenGyre, bringing elastic RL to extreme-long-horizon (XLong) agent training. ✨
